# Configuration

Run `tg help config` for the complete reference below. The aliases
`tg config help`, `tg config --help`, and `tg config -h` print the same help.
These commands work without credentials and do not read or create configuration files.

## Configuration files and editor support

The default directory is `~/.config/tg-cli`; set `TG_CTL_CONFIG_DIR` to use a
different directory. Settings live in `config.yaml`, while Telegram credentials
live in the separate `.env` file managed by `tg auth`.

Normal configuration reads and writes refresh `config.schema.json` beside the
YAML file and maintain this leading comment:

```yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=./config.schema.json
```

The YAML language server resolves this relative path from the YAML file's
directory. Editors using that server can provide key completion, descriptions,
and diagnostics. The comment is ignored by the runtime configuration readers.
For editor behavior, see the [YAML language server documentation](https://github.com/redhat-developer/yaml-language-server#using-a-modeline).

If the configuration is missing, a normal configuration read creates the
annotated file and schema. Help and dry-run paths do not initialize these files.
Metadata refresh is best-effort: a readable configuration remains usable if its
directory cannot be updated. Updating the modeline preserves the remaining YAML
text, including user comments; settings are not parsed and serialized again.

The schema describes the recommended scalar syntax and flags unknown keys.
It supplies editor guidance; existing runtime parsing and fallback behavior stay
the same. Use unquoted `true` and `false`, decimal integers, and one-level
settings inside the documented blocks. The reference explains legacy accepted
forms and the few fields whose defaults are chosen at runtime.

## Complete reference

```text
tg configuration reference

Configuration: ~/.config/tg-cli/config.yaml
Editor schema: ~/.config/tg-cli/config.schema.json
Set TG_CTL_CONFIG_DIR to select a different configuration directory.
The schema is refreshed beside config.yaml during configuration reads/writes.
Editor modeline: # yaml-language-server: $schema=./config.schema.json

Precedence and credentials
  Runtime defaults are overridden by config.yaml. Feature flags are then
  overridden by --feature NAME / --no-feature NAME (--no-feature wins a tie).
  Credentials live in ~/.config/tg-cli/.env: TG_BOT_TOKEN and TG_CHAT_ID.
  The shell environment overrides .env values. Set up credentials with tg auth.

control.enabled scope
  This only gates tg's lazy autostart after an agent send inside tmux.
  It does not turn off buttons, registrations, OS autostart, or a running daemon.
  Explicit tg-ctl run and tg-ctl start still work. Use tg-ctl stop to stop the
  daemon now, or tg-ctl disable to remove OS autostart and stop it.

Remote ctl server (control.server, control.machine, control.remote_machines)
  One bot has one tg-ctl poller. A second machine runs agents against it instead of its own:
    client machine:       control: server: "ssh://tg-ctl-ubuntu" and machine: "clvm"
    daemon host (server): control: remote_machines: "clvm=ultra@clvm.example.com"
  A machine is a client or the daemon host, never both. With none of the three keys
  behaviour is unchanged. Any of them present but invalid makes every tg send
  (--dry-run included), tg-ctl run/start/restart/enable and tg config validate fail
  with the diagnostic (exit 78 / 1); there is no silent fallback to local behavior.
  An empty value ("") counts as unset.
  The rules live in tg-remote config check, which runs offline (no network, no ssh).

File syntax and compatibility
  Use top-level control:, voice:, features:, and laya: blocks with one-level scalar
  entries. The editor schema recommends unquoted true/false and plain decimal
  integers. The runtime also accepts unquoted yes/no, on/off, and 1/0 booleans.
  Only voice.enabled accepts quoted booleans; control and features do not.
  voice.threads also accepts quoted numeric values; control integer values
  must be unquoted decimal digits. Invalid values usually retain defaults.
  Unknown control/voice keys are ignored; unknown feature names are retained
  by the feature parser but do not add a feature. The schema flags unknown
  keys to catch mistakes. Full YAML constructs and YAML arrays are unsupported.
  Omit unused blocks; use control.enabled: false or voice.enabled: false
  for their respective opt-outs. The laya: block is stricter: an unknown key, a
  non-boolean value, a non-positive timeout, a relative task_bin or socket, or required: true
  together with enabled: false (or TG_LAYA=0) is an error (exit 78 where Laya is
  consulted), never healed into a default.

Laya (the local model behind the report checks)
  tg asks Laya about explicit problem reports and about bodies in which the
  deterministic detector found no question. When no server answers, tg runs
  `task classify-server start` once (a failed start is not retried for 300 s), then
  asks with the warm timeout. To start it yourself: task classify-server start
  Environment overrides config.yaml: TG_LAYA (0/false/no/off disables),
  TG_LAYA_AUTOSTART, TG_LAYA_REQUIRED, TG_LAYA_TIMEOUT_MS (warm_timeout_ms),
  TG_LAYA_COLD_TIMEOUT_SEC (cold_timeout_sec) and TG_LAYA_SOCKET (laya.socket: use exactly
  this socket; it is never autostarted, no model is started for it). TG_PYTHON picks the interpreter that runs the caller.
  Unavailable Laya, for any reason, prints a hint naming the reason, what was tried
  and the next step. With laya.required: true the send fails instead (exit 1, before
  any Telegram request). --dry-run never starts, connects to or loads Laya.

Validation
  tg config validate checks config.yaml read-only: no credentials, network, or
  file changes; a missing file is valid. Errors (exit 1) are unknown keys, values
  the runtime ignores or heals (wrong type, enum, or range), unreadable or
  non-mapping files, and YAML the one-level readers skip (inline blocks, nested
  mappings, duplicates, inconsistent indentation, quoted section names, empty
  sections) and quoted escapes the runtime keeps literally (\t, '').
  A final syntax pass runs Bun.YAML.parse (Bun 1.2.21 or newer; older Bun skips it
  with a warning) and rejects text the line checks did not model.
  Warnings (exit 0) are legacy forms the runtime accepts but the editor schema
  flags: yes/no, on/off, 1/0 booleans and quoted voice.enabled/voice.threads.
  control.server, control.machine and control.remote_machines are checked by the offline
  tg-remote config check (python3, no network, no ssh); a bad value, or a checker that
  cannot run while any of them is set, is an error (exit 1).
  The laya: block is checked by the Python caller (python3 -I <repo>/tg-laya
  check-config) with the same rules the send path applies; it needs python3 3.12+.

Example config.yaml (credentials stay in .env):
# yaml-language-server: $schema=./config.schema.json
control:
  enabled: true
  idle_exit_min: 15
voice:
  enabled: false
features:
  autolink-msgrefs: true

control:
  Inbound control and daemon settings.

  control.enabled (boolean)
    Default: true
    Allow tg's lazy autostart of tg-ctl after a successful send from a detected agent inside tmux. This switch does not disable buttons or registrations, stop a running daemon, or block explicit daemon starts.
    Example: enabled: true

  control.transport (string; auto | tmux | channel)
    Default: "auto"
    Legacy transport selector. auto and tmux retain the current routing; channel is reserved and currently logs a warning and falls back to tmux.
    Example: transport: "auto"
    Example: transport: "tmux"

  control.session (string)
    Default: unset (auto-discover)
    Pin tmux discovery to this session name. An explicit session registration from tg-ctl start --session takes precedence; omit to auto-discover.
    Example: session: "agents"

  control.inject_wrap (string)
    Default: "[TG from {name} {id}] {msg}"
    Template around inbound text. Placeholders: {name} is the sender name, {msg} is the message text, and {id} is its tg# message reference.
    Example: inject_wrap: "[TG from {name} {id}] {msg}"

  control.staleness_sec (integer; minimum 1)
    Default: 300
    Legacy age setting in seconds, retained for compatibility. The daemon does not drop inbound messages by age.
    Example: staleness_sec: 600

  control.idle_exit_min (integer; minimum 1)
    Default: 30
    Minutes without a live agent before the daemon exits. Agents outside tmux and recent registrations also count as activity.
    Example: idle_exit_min: 15

  control.allowed_senders (string or integer; minimum 0)
    Default: ""
    Additional allowed Telegram user IDs as a comma-separated scalar (for example "123, 456") or a single integer. An empty string adds none. YAML arrays are not supported.
    Example: allowed_senders: "123456789, 987654321"
    Example: allowed_senders: 123456789

  control.topics (boolean)
    Default: false
    Enable forum-topic routing in a supergroup. Requires a forum supergroup with the bot allowed to manage topics.
    Example: topics: false

  control.private_topics (boolean)
    Default: false
    Enable topics for sessions in a private bot chat. If the bot lacks the private-topic capability, session creation asks whether to continue without topics or cancel. Topic-creation API errors fall back to flat-chat behavior with a diagnostic.
    Example: private_topics: false

  control.git_state_banner (boolean)
    Default: true
    Prepend a warning when a fresh non-reply message is automatically routed into a pane whose repository has uncommitted changes or a non-main branch.
    Example: git_state_banner: true

  control.server (string)
    Default: unset (this machine is not a ctl client)
    Client machine only: the ssh_config alias of the host that runs tg-ctl, as ssh://<alias> (alias or host name only: no user, port, path or leading dash; key, port, jump host and host-key pinning belong in ~/.ssh/config). Setting it makes this machine a ctl client: tg-ctl run/start/restart/enable exit 78 and tg never autostarts a daemon. Requires control.machine; a machine is a client or the daemon host, never both.
    Example: server: "ssh://tg-ctl-ubuntu"

  control.machine (string)
    Default: unset (required when control.server is set)
    Client machine only: this machine's name in the server's routes and history, 1-32 characters of a-z, 0-9 and -, starting with a letter. Required with control.server.
    Example: machine: "clvm"

  control.remote_machines (string)
    Default: unset (no client machines)
    Daemon host only: comma-separated name=ssh-target list of the client machines this tg-ctl serves (at most 8, unique names; target is [user@]host). It is both the allowlist of peers and the address replies are delivered to. Not allowed together with control.server or control.machine.
    Example: remote_machines: "clvm=ultra@clvm.example.com"

voice:
  Local transcription of inbound voice notes.

  voice.enabled (boolean)
    Default: false
    Enable local transcription of inbound voice notes. A usable binary and model are required; tg voice setup discovers or installs them and writes this block. An explicit false opts out of automatic setup.
    Example: enabled: false

  voice.runner (string; whisper.cpp | faster-whisper)
    Default: "whisper.cpp"
    Local Whisper runner. whisper.cpp uses a native executable; faster-whisper uses a Python environment. Setup may choose a runner suited to the host.
    Example: runner: "whisper.cpp"
    Example: runner: "faster-whisper"

  voice.bin_path (string)
    Default: ""
    Path to whisper-cli (or its legacy main executable) for whisper.cpp, or to the virtual-environment Python executable for faster-whisper.
    Example: bin_path: "/opt/whisper/bin/whisper-cli"

  voice.model_path (string)
    Default: ""
    Path to a ggml model file for whisper.cpp, or a model-size token (such as large-v3-turbo) or converted model directory for faster-whisper.
    Example: model_path: "/opt/whisper/models/ggml-base.bin"
    Example: model_path: "large-v3-turbo"

  voice.language (string)
    Default: "auto"
    Language token passed to the runner, or auto for automatic language detection. An empty value resolves to auto.
    Example: language: "en"
    Example: language: "auto"

  voice.threads (integer; minimum 1)
    Default: unset (physical core count)
    CPU thread count. Omit to use the physical core count. A custom faster-whisper transcription script must accept --threads when this setting is supplied.
    Example: threads: 4

features:
  Outbound feature flags. --feature and --no-feature override these values.

  features.autolink-tasks (boolean)
    Default: true
    Resolve Linear task references and add task links and titles to outbound messages.
    Example: autolink-tasks: true

  features.autolink-prs (boolean)
    Default: true
    Resolve GitHub issue and pull-request references against the current repository and add links and titles.
    Example: autolink-prs: true

  features.autolink-msgrefs (boolean)
    Default: true
    Recognize tg# message references and link them when the chat supports a message URL.
    Example: autolink-msgrefs: true

  features.autolink-msgref-preview (boolean)
    Default: true
    Quote a referenced Telegram message inline when local history contains it. Requires autolink-msgrefs.
    Example: autolink-msgref-preview: true

  features.md-as-pdf (boolean)
    Default: true
    Convert explicitly attached Markdown files to PDF for readable Telegram previews.
    Example: md-as-pdf: true

  features.code-as-pdf (boolean)
    Default: true
    Convert explicitly attached code and configuration files to a mobile-sized, highlighted PDF. --with-original and --no-pdf adjust attachment behavior.
    Example: code-as-pdf: true

  features.attach-denylist (boolean)
    Default: true
    Refuse explicit attachments that look like secret files, including environment files, keys, and credentials.
    Example: attach-denylist: true

  features.flood-cap (boolean)
    Default: true
    Limit the number of Telegram messages produced by one fragmented send.
    Example: flood-cap: true

  features.cjk-guard (boolean)
    Default: true
    Reject isolated CJK characters inside otherwise Latin or Cyrillic words and mixed-script garbage tokens; ordinary CJK text remains supported.
    Example: cjk-guard: true

  features.screenshot-guard (boolean)
    Default: true
    Require a photo attachment when the caption or title claims to show a screenshot.
    Example: screenshot-guard: true

  features.file-mention-guard (boolean)
    Default: true
    Refuse an agent message that names an existing local document without attaching it, and suggest the explicit --file command.
    Example: file-mention-guard: true

  features.hooks (boolean)
    Default: true
    Run pre-send-photo hooks when hook descriptors are installed. AGENTS_HOOKS=0 bypasses these hooks.
    Example: hooks: true

laya:
  Laya, the local model tg asks about reports. tg starts it when it is not running. Read and validated by the Python caller (src/tgcli/laya): an invalid block exits 78 where Laya is consulted.

  laya.enabled (boolean)
    Default: true
    Ask Laya about reports at all. false (or TG_LAYA=0) switches the model off: the deterministic checks decide alone and no hint is printed on the ask path. Incompatible with required: true.
    Example: enabled: true

  laya.autostart (boolean)
    Default: true
    When no live Laya server answers, start one with `task classify-server start` (bounded by cold_timeout_sec). A failed start is not retried for 300 seconds. TG_LAYA_AUTOSTART overrides. --dry-run never starts anything.
    Example: autostart: true

  laya.required (boolean)
    Default: false
    Fail a send (exit 1, before any Telegram request) when Laya was consulted and is unavailable for any reason, instead of falling back to the deterministic checks with a hint. TG_LAYA_REQUIRED overrides. Cannot be combined with enabled: false or TG_LAYA=0 (exit 78).
    Example: required: false

  laya.cold_timeout_sec (integer; minimum 1)
    Default: 75
    Seconds allowed for the autostart (spawn plus model load). Measured cold start: 6.4 s on a CPU host; task classify-server start itself waits up to 60 s, so the default leaves room for its own diagnostic. TG_LAYA_COLD_TIMEOUT_SEC overrides.
    Example: cold_timeout_sec: 75
    Example: cold_timeout_sec: 120

  laya.warm_timeout_ms (integer; minimum 1)
    Default: 3000
    Milliseconds allowed for one request to a running server. Measured warm calls: 31-64 ms (GPU/fast host), 267-1395 ms (CPU host, the first call being the slowest). TG_LAYA_TIMEOUT_MS overrides.
    Example: warm_timeout_ms: 3000
    Example: warm_timeout_ms: 2000

  laya.task_bin (string)
    Default: unset (task is searched on trusted PATH entries)
    Absolute path of the task executable used for autostart. Without it tg searches PATH entries that are absolute, not world-writable and owned by you or root, never the current directory. A path that is relative, missing or not executable is an error, not a fallback.
    Example: task_bin: "/usr/local/bin/task"

  laya.socket (string)
    Default: unset (tg discovers laya-*.sock under task-cli's classify directory)
    Absolute path of a private Unix socket served by an external Laya (for example a proxy to another machine). Pins it durably: tg uses exactly this socket, never starts `task` or any model for it, and an unreachable pinned socket is an unavailable Laya (with laya.required: true the send fails). The parent directory must be owned by you with no group/other access and the socket must be yours. Relative, empty or `..`-containing values are an error (exit 78). TG_LAYA_SOCKET overrides.
    Example: socket: "/run/user/1000/tg-cli/laya.sock"
```

## Maintaining the generated files

The registry in [features/config/schema.ts](../features/config/schema.ts) supplies
CLI help and the schema, with defaults imported from the runtime modules. To
regenerate both this reference and the tracked schema:

```bash
bun run schema:gen
bun run schema:check
```

The check reports missing or stale artifacts without rewriting them. CI runs it,
and the ordinary test suite compares both tracked artifacts to the generator so
the existing remote shipping test gate also catches drift.

This repository runs Bun scripts directly and has no build step. Installation
links the checkout, and deployment fast-forwards its tracked files, so the schema
ships through those existing paths. Generation is explicit; it never stages or
commits files automatically.
